interest: This docket list is historically compelling because it captures the diplomatic maneuvering surrounding the ill-fated 1940 Tokyo Olympic Games—the "Missing Olympics"—which were eventually forfeited by Japan in 1938 due to the Second Sino-Japanese War and reallocated to Helsinki before being cancelled entirely due to World War II. It provides valuable insight into the intersection of international sports, soft power, and geopolitical tensions in the late 1930s, highlighting how Japanese envoys like judo founder Jigoro Kano and Count Michimasa Soejima lobbied internationally, while American citizens and diplomats weighed the propriety of participating in games hosted by an increasingly militaristic Japan. Additionally, it illuminates complex diplomatic questions of the era, including the contested Olympic participation of the unrecognized puppet state of Manchukuo, trademark regulations governing the five-ring Olympic emblem, and an intriguing cross-reference linking foreign-Japanese romantic relationships to alleged espionage.
overview: This file contains the Department of State's docket sheet (List of Papers) for decimal file classification 894.4063, cataloguing diplomatic correspondence, memoranda, and cross-reference sheets concerning Japan and the Olympic Games from July 1936 to 1938. The register tracks Japan's campaign to secure and host the 1940 XII Olympic Games in Tokyo, recording customs courtesies arranged for Olympic invitations commissioner Jigoro Kano and visits by Count Michimasa Soejima. It also indexes reports and cross-references regarding the geopolitical ramifications of the Tokyo Games, including German Army preparations, trademark protections for the Olympic five-ring emblem, American debates over the propriety of participation, the potential inclusion of the unrecognized state of Manchukuo, and early indications of Japan's inability to host, pointing toward a transfer of the Games to Helsinki, Finland.

subfiles.summary: This two-page docket sheet registers official correspondence, despatches, and cross-reference sheets concerning the Olympic Games under file 894.4063 between July 1936 and 1938. It records courtesies and diplomatic coordination for Japanese delegates Jigoro Kano and Count Michimasa Soejima during the campaign for and organization of the 1940 Tokyo Olympics. It further summarizes incoming reports on German athletic preparations, queries regarding Olympic trademark protections, political questions surrounding Manchukuo's participation, American domestic debate over participation, and the potential relocation of the games to Helsinki.
